# Daily AI Newsletter Digest - 21/1/2026

## 🔥 Top Stories
- The US and Taiwan have agreed on a $250B deal to bolster domestic chip production, with TSMC leading the initiative.
- OpenAI has reached $20B in annualized revenue and is introducing targeted ads to ChatGPT, while also facing a $134B lawsuit from Elon Musk.
- Mark Zuckerberg's metaverse push is winding down, with Meta shifting focus from VR to AI-powered wearables, including smart glasses.

## 🤖 AI Models & Research
- GLM-4.7 Flash, an open-source model, has been updated with significant improvements in coding, agent, and reasoning benchmarks.
- Z.ai has released a 30B coding model, GLM-4.7-Flash, which outperforms similarly-sized open-source rivals.
- Modulate's Ensemble Listening Models (ELMs) can decode intent, emotion, and authenticity in audio, with Velma, their ELM, now publicly available.
- Researchers have developed a deep learning-based system for fall detection using wearable inertial sensors, achieving high accuracy and speed.

## 🛠️ Tools & Products
- Claude Code allows users to teach Claude once and have it remember forever, applicable for various tasks and workflows.
- Vibecode has released a new app generation platform powered by Claude Code, enabling one-click web deployment.
- Google Stitch is adding API key management and PRD generation for product managers.
- QA Wolf's AI-native solution provides high-volume, high-speed test coverage for web and mobile apps.
- Slack has introduced a new personal agent called Slackbot, built directly into the Slack workspace.

## 📰 Industry News
- Elon Musk has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging that the company violated its original nonprofit mission.
- The UK financial system is heavily reliant on AI, but regulation has not kept pace, posing risks to consumers and financial stability.
- The New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) is building a digital trading platform using blockchain technology for 24/7 trading of tokenized stocks and ETFs.
- China has blocked Nvidia's H200 chips at the border, despite the US clearing them for export with conditions.

## 📚 Resources & Learning
- Mindstream has created a mini-course to master prompt engineering in 7 days, covering topics from basic prompts to advanced techniques.
- The Code by Superhuman provides resources for learning Claude Code, becoming a great engineering leader, and staying up-to-date with the latest AI/ML research papers.
- TLDR is hiring a Senior Software Engineer, Applied AI, and offers a referral program with rewards.
- JournalClub.io provides a platform for discussing and learning from AI research papers, with a focus on practical applications.

## World of AI Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- GLM-4.7 Flash, an open-source model, has been updated with significant improvements in coding, agent, and reasoning benchmarks, posing a challenge to Gemini 3 Flash.
- The update focuses on efficiency, reliability, and real-world usefulness, making it a viable option for those seeking a balance between performance and cost.
- The model is designed for "real-world deployment" and is suitable for building coding tools, agents, and deploying models locally or on limited hardware.

### Detailed Points
- **GLM-4.7 Flash Update**: The latest update to GLM-4.7 Flash brings substantial gains in coding and agent benchmarks such as SWE-bench Verified, TauBench v2, and BrowserComp, showcasing its ability to perform tasks beyond just dialogue.
- **Efficiency and Performance**: It offers a smaller footprint, lower latency, and easier deployment while maintaining competitive performance on serious benchmarks, making it an attractive option for practical applications.
- **Use Cases**: This model is particularly suited for individuals and organizations working on coding tools, agents, or deploying models in resource-constrained environments, and for those who prioritize efficiency and cost-effectiveness without compromising on performance.
- **Comparison to Gemini 3 Flash**: GLM-4.7 Flash's improvements put pressure on Gemini 3 Flash, especially in terms of efficiency and practical usability, suggesting a shift towards models that offer a balance between size, cost, and performance.
- **Reasoning Performance**: Despite its focus on efficiency, GLM-4.7 Flash holds its own against larger models in reasoning benchmarks like AIME 25 and GPQA, demonstrating its thoughtful and reliable nature.
- **Partnership and Tools**: The newsletter mentions a partnership with HubSpot, highlighting the use of AI in tools like HubSpot Smart CRM for efficient pipeline management and deal tracking.

## TAAFT - There's An AI For That

### Key Highlights
- China has blocked Nvidia chips after the US approved them for export with conditions.
- Notion is developing AI agents that can control your browser and other tools.
- Tesla is restarting its Dojo supercomputer project with a focus on space-based AI compute.
- Google has published a prompting guide organized by job role to help with AI adoption.
- A company called DEEP Robotics has developed a firefighting squad of robodogs.

### Detailed Points
- China has blocked Nvidia's H200 chips at the border, despite the US clearing them for export with conditions. Chinese customs have also warned domestic tech firms against buying the chips unless necessary.
- Notion is testing AI agent capabilities, including custom MCPs, Workers for building automations, and connectors for Calendar, Mail, and third-party tools.
- Tesla's Dojo3 project will focus on space-based AI compute, joining the growing push for orbital data centers.
- Google's prompting guide provides fundamentals for AI adoption, organized by job function, to make it easier to apply AI in various roles.
- DEEP Robotics has developed a firefighting squad of robodogs that can navigate rubble, detect gas leaks, and locate trapped people using thermal imaging and LiDAR.
- Other updates include the development of Anam, a visual editor for designing directly in React apps, and RewarxStudio, which transforms simple product snapshots into studio-quality commercial photos and 4K videos.
- Nume is an AI-powered financial tool that connects to QuickBooks or Xero and provides proactive analysis, smart Slack alerts, and quick answers on burn rate, runway, and variances.
- The newsletter also mentions various AI tools, including TheLibrarian, Base44, GLM-4.7-Flash, and STEP3-VL-10B, which offer features such as visual editing, app development, and multimodal modeling.

newsletters.summary:
## The Rundown AI

### Key Highlights
- Claude Code sparks 'selfware' era, with Anthropic's tool fueling a wave of AI-built software creation
- Ex-OpenAI policy lead launches new AI safety nonprofit, AVERI, to promote independent third-party audits of frontier AI models
- Optimize prompting with a Markdown strategy to improve AI performance
- Anthropic releases its first Economic Index of 2026, providing insights into AI adoption and productivity gains

### Detailed Points
- Claude Code is having its "ChatGPT moment" among both developers and hobbyists, with the viral excitement fueling a selloff in traditional software stocks and investors fearing a new era of AI-built 'selfware.'
- A Morgan Stanley SaaS index is down 15% YTD, with stocks from major software companies like Intuit, Adobe, and Salesforce dropping double digits.
- Vercel’s CTO used Claude to finish a year-long project in a week; another CEO scrapped plans to hire engineers after the tool made him ‘5x more productive’.
- Others went viral for building apps entirely with Claude Code, from custom MRI viewers to handling self-sustaining tomato growth.
- Ex-OpenAI policy lead Miles Brundage launched AVERI, a nonprofit pushing for independent third-party audits of frontier AI models instead of letting labs self-certify their own safety claims.
- AVERI will focus on establishing audit standards and policies rather than conducting evaluations itself, acting as a ‘think tank’ over an actual auditor.
- The nonprofit published a framework of "AI Assurance Levels" — ranging from today's self-testing (Level 1) to treaty-grade international verification (Level 4).
- You.com released a guide on how to extract any completed AI task into reusable markdown instructions, making valuable tasks portable and repeatable across any AI tool.
- Anthropic published its fourth Economic Index, providing a deep dive into 2M Claude chats and revealing that most AI usage still looks more like collaboration than replacement, with humans in the driver's seat for the majority of tasks.
- AI handles around 1/4 of tasks in almost 50% of all jobs, up from 36% last year, but full role replacement is happening at under 10% of firms.
- Tasks requiring high-school skills are sped up 9x faster with AI, and 12x for college-level tasks, with Claude’s gains increasing for difficult use cases.
- Z AI released GLM-4.7-Flash, a 30B, speed and efficiency-focused variant of its powerful open-source model.
- Business insights firm Gartner projected that worldwide AI spending will reach $2.52T in 2026, a 44% jump driven largely by massive infrastructure buildouts.
- South Korea is holding an AI competition to elevate the country’s top homegrown AI models, with LG, SK, and startup Upstage remaining in contention.
- xAI engineer Sulaiman Ghori announced that he left the company, coming on the heels of a revealing viral interview detailing the startup’s inner workings.

## claude skills 101

### Key Highlights
- Claude Skills allow users to teach Claude once and have it remember forever, applicable for various tasks and workflows.
- There are two ways to build a Claude Skill: the Quick Way using the skill-creator tool and the Custom Way by building it manually.
- Claude Skills can be used for tasks such as processing meeting notes, drafting email responses, and more.

### Detailed Points
- **Introduction to Claude Skills**: A skill is a set of instructions that Claude remembers and applies on its own, allowing for efficient task management and automation.
- **Building the First Skill**: The Quick Way involves using the skill-creator tool, while the Custom Way requires manual building for more complex workflows.
- **Method 1: Quick Way (Skill-Creator Tool)**: This method uses a meta-skill called "creator-skill" to generate other skills. It involves defining decision logic and letting Claude encode it.
- **Method 2: Custom Way (Manual Build)**: This method requires a specific structure and is more suitable for complex workflows. It involves creating files, writing the skill, and uploading it to Claude.
- **CES 2026 Roundup**: The newsletter mentions a roundup of CES 2026, highlighting new technologies and innovations.
- **Tools that Caught Attention**: 
  - **northr.ai**: An adaptive planning tool for knowledge workers and founders.
  - **Aident AI**: A tool that compiles workflows into a working "Playbook" (scripts + prompts) and connects over 250 tools.
  - **Noodle Seed**: A no-code platform that turns websites into AI-ready apps inside ChatGPT.
- **Using Skills and Projects Together**: Combining skills and projects allows for consistent application of logic without restating context or correcting outputs.
- **Personal Take**: The author believes that skills will be effective because they are instructions that are repeatable and dependable, unlike previous attempts at creating AI personalities.

## JournalClub.io

### Key Highlights
- Researchers from the National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST) in Pakistan have developed a deep learning-based system for fall detection using wearable inertial sensors.
- The system can identify falls during pre-impact, post-impact, and transition phases with an average inference time of 20 milliseconds.
- The model outperforms existing methods in scalability, accuracy, and inference time, achieving F1-scores around 98% and specificity consistently near 99%.
- The system uses a hybrid CNN-LSTM-Attention framework and is trained on the KFall dataset, which contains data from people with a nine-axis inertial sensor mounted on their lower back.

### Detailed Points
- The researchers aimed to improve fall detection systems, which are crucial for saving lives, especially among the elderly population.
- Falls can be divided into distinct phases: pre-impact, post-impact, and transition, and most existing systems only detect falls after they have happened (post-impact).
- The proposed system uses a lower-back IMU sensor, which provides more accurate data than wrist-mounted sensors, but may be less convenient for real-world deployment.
- The system's architecture consists of a one-dimensional convolutional layer, batch normalization, two parallel convolutional layers with different sampling strategies, a two-layer stacked LSTM, and a multi-head self-attention layer.
- The model is trained on the KFall dataset, which includes  daily activities and 15 types of simulated falls, and the authors computed post-impact phase labels by analyzing the rate of change in acceleration.
- The system's performance is evaluated separately on the three phases, and it achieves high precision, recall, F1-score, and specificity across all 36 classes.
- The authors provide architectural diagrams, preprocessing breakdowns, full confusion matrices, and ablation studies, making the paper a valuable resource for researchers working on fall detection systems.
- The system's speed and accuracy come from careful scope control and architectural restraint, but may have practical limits for deployment on constrained hardware.

## The Code by Superhuman

### Key Highlights
- Ryan Dahl, creator of Node.js, declared that the era of humans writing code is over, and the key skill is no longer syntax but orchestrating agents.
- OpenAI introduced ads to ChatGPT, but developers can breathe easy as API, Business, and Enterprise users won't see any ads.
- Z.ai dropped a powerful 30B coding model, GLM-4.7-Flash, which outperforms similarly-sized open-source rivals.

### Detailed Points
- Ryan Dahl's statement sparked a debate in the tech community, with some leaders framing it as the next natural abstraction layer in software's evolution, similar to when compilers replaced assembly language.
- OpenAI's ads will appear after responses as UI elements, ensuring query responses won't be influenced by advertisers.
- GLM-4.7-Flash handles both frontend and backend tasks, with weights available on HuggingFace and free API access.
- Other notable updates include the release of Opus 4.5, which wrote 200 PRs for Boris Cherny, creator of Claude Code, and the launch of Openwork, an open-source computer-use agent that is ~4x faster than Claude for browser tasks.
- The newsletter also covers trends and insights, including what separates great engineering teams from the rest, how to use Plan mode for coding, and 8 strategies for online job hunting.

newsletters.summary:
## Superhuman

### Key Highlights
- OpenAI has reached $20B in annual recurring revenue, a 233% jump from the previous year.
- Vibecode has released a new app generation platform powered by Claude Code, allowing for one-click web deployment.
- Black Forest Labs has released open-source models (4B and 9B parameters) that create images in under 0.5 seconds on modern hardware.
- Slack has introduced a new personal agent called Slackbot, built directly into the Slack workspace.

### Detailed Points
- OpenAI's revenue growth is attributed to the company's expansion in compute capacity from 0.6 to 1.9 GWs.
- Vibecode's platform uses Claude Code to transform plain-English prompts into web and mobile apps with responsive frontends, backends, and database setups.
- The open-source models released by Black Forest Labs can be used commercially without any costs, with the 4B parameter version shipped under Apache 2.0.
- Slackbot handles busywork by understanding the user's work, collaborators, and communication style, and can be used to search messages, files, people, and workflow history.
- Slackbot also allows users to chat with it like a teammate and get all the power of AI with enterprise-grade security.
- A researcher has built an AI-coded advent calendar using "vibe coding" that has gone viral on social media.
- A creator has released a 5-hour masterclass on how to use Claude, a popular AI tool.
- The Superhuman team has shared their top 125 AI tools and top 1,000 prompts for better prompting.

## TLDR AI

### Key Highlights
- Anthropic is working on knowledge bases for Claude, allowing it to reference and update information.
- Google Stitch is adding API key management and PRD generation for product managers.

- **Character.ai's Slonk**: Character.ai uses an internal system called Slonk to manage GPU research clusters, merging the flexibility of Kubernetes with the productivity of HPC environments.
- **Training CLI Agents**: Nvidia showcases how to train AI agents for command-line tasks using synthetic data and reinforcement learning.
- **AI Engineering**: AI teams struggle with deploying agents due to the lack of standardized runtime infrastructure, leaving each team to reinvent complex infrastructure from scratch.
- **LLMs and Careers**: With the rise of LLMs, companies seek professionals with deep fundamental knowledge, and AI will make services ubiquitous and embedded in everything.

## Mindstream

### Key Highlights
- Mark Zuckerberg's metaverse push is winding down due to years of failing to make virtual reality profitable.
- Meta is shifting focus from VR to AI-powered wearables, including smart glasses.
- The UK financial system is heavily reliant on AI, but regulation has not kept pace, posing risks to consumers and financial stability.
- Mindstream reader poll results show mixed opinions on the metaverse and AI in finance.

### Detailed Points
- Meta's metaverse experiment is coming to an end, with the company laying off around 1,500 employees from its Reality Labs division, which develops VR and AR products.
- Three VR game studios are being closed, while Horizon Worlds will continue operating on a smaller scale.
- Meta's smart glasses are the new focus, but their future remains uncertain due to inventory issues, market saturation, and potential regulatory hurdles.
- A parliamentary committee has warned that delays in managing AI risks could expose consumers and the UK financial system to serious harm, citing a lack of transparency and accountability in AI-driven decisions.
- Over 75% of City firms now use AI, particularly insurers and international banks, for tasks such as automating admin work, processing insurance claims, and assessing creditworthiness.
- The committee is calling for faster action, including AI-focused stress tests and clearer guidance from the Financial Conduct Authority on how consumer protection rules apply to AI use.
- Rockstar Games has confirmed that its Rockstar North studio in Edinburgh has reopened after a boiler malfunction.
- Amazon has confirmed cases of latent tuberculosis at its Coventry warehouse, prompting screenings and NHS involvement.
